examples.knowledge_point: Finding All Subsets of a Given Set
examples.problem: Find all of the subsets of $A = \{ a, b, c \}.$
examples.worked_solution:
To find every subset of $A,$ we list out every combination of elements within $A.$ 

We can use the following diagram to visualize the process:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071627/assets/8323a4292a4f06d66d456bfce1906cbc7e9933a3fac41dd5fb643e13d25f6a6e.png)

Note that we must include the empty set since it is a subset of every set.

By doing this, we get

$$
\emptyset, \{a\}, \{b\}, \{c\}, \{a, b\}, \{a, c\}, \{b, c\}, \{a, b, c\}.
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following sets is a subset of $A={1,2,3,4}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
A set is a subset of $A$ if all its elements are elements of $A.$

Notice that the empty set ${}$ is a subset of any set.

Therefore, ${}$ is a subset of $A.$
